absent: Numeric values and bit layout of depot flag mask, acquiring flag and allocation permission flag.
Concrete cursor, node and mark-constant definitions for the indexed array beyond the routed accessors.
Full field layouts for tracker, tracker directory, stack record and handle-parts structures.
Hash seed value, table sizing, pool sizing, alignment, frame-limit and quarantine capacity parameters.
Lifecycle of the debug filesystem directory and dead-mark constant beyond the routed read path.
Error-token encoding and sequential-file integration beyond the call sites shown.
Initial counter values and sizing policy for quarantine accounting.

findings.text: Provides mark-setting on an indexed slot that is occupied; empty slots are left unchanged.
Provides guarded lookup of an indexed entry with retry handling, normalizing zero-valued entries to null.
Provides mark query that proceeds downward while the current level reports the mark and succeeds only on reaching a non-node entry.
Invalid cursor reports mark absent; root-only cursor reflects array-level mark and nested cursor reflects node slot mark.
Defines a small output abstraction carrying a dispatch routine, a prefix string, an optional bounded buffer with capacity and fill count, and an optional sequential sink.
Each rendering path selects one sink behavior through the dispatch routine: kernel logging, bounded buffer append with truncation-aware accounting, or sequential output.

Aggregates live trackers by allocation handle, counting every entry in the total and per-handle frequencies for distinct handles up to the caller limit, skipping further distinct handles beyond the limit.
Statistics collection reports an out-of-memory error token when its flexible allocation cannot be satisfied.
Renders per-handle usage summaries with totals and a skipped remainder; it stays silent for an empty directory and emits a diagnostic when statistics are unavailable.
Shared directory rendering requires the directory lock to be held by the caller.
Provides locked, interrupt-safe locked, and bounded-buffer wrappers around the shared directory rendering core.
Public print and bounded formatting paths acquire the directory spinlock with interrupt state saved and restore it after rendering.

Allocation path registers a new tracker with a saved allocation stack and list insertion; a missing handle pointer or allocation failure instead increments a fallback counter and returns the corresponding status.

Release path captures a freeing stack, flags the object dead, moves it to quarantine, and either retires the oldest quarantined object when no capacity remains or consumes one capacity unit; missing handle or object adjusts fallback counters.
Teardown marks the directory dead before locking, drains quarantine storage, reports and discards any remaining live trackers as a leak indication, then validates fallback counters.

A second release of the same tracker is detected through its dead flag, produces allocation and free location diagnostics where available, warns, and returns an invalid-argument status without further list mutation.
The debug filesystem coordination hook for teardown is a no-operation in the routed configuration.
The debug directory reference starts as a negative no-entry sentinel value.

Debug filesystem read validates the directory handle and liveness mark under xarray locking, then acquires the directory lock before releasing the xarray lock in an interrupt-safe sequence; invalid or dead handles yield a no-data status.
Debug filesystem operations bind open to a per-directory single-open show path with sequential read, seek and release helpers.
Provides a deduplicating persistent handle for a stack trace after interrupt filtering, hashing and bucket lookup, with optional allocation permission in the flagged variant.
Saving attempts a lock-free lookup first, prepares pool memory outside the lock, then repeats the lookup under the lock before inserting, avoiding concurrently inserted duplicates.
Insertion synchronizes on the pool raw spinlock with interrupt state saved; non-maskable interrupt or non-spinning contexts use a best-effort trylock path and never allocate.
Bucket selection hashes the whole entry sequence with a fixed seed; equality requires matching hash and length plus element-wise equality.
Bucket scanning runs under a non-tracing scheduler read-side section and, for acquiring requests, returns only records whose reference can be taken as nonzero.

Record creation truncates overlong traces, reuses a freelist object for the refcounted flavor or consumes pool space otherwise, copies entries, and initializes a saturated count for persistent records versus a unit count for refcounted records with matching statistics.
Pool allocation and freelist helpers require the pool lock held; the handle fetch path requires that lock not held.

Pool exhaustion installs prepared memory while under the capacity limit, publishes the pool reference before bumping the count, resets the offset, and retains surplus prepared memory for later use; reaching the limit warns and fails.
Handles encode a one-based pool index plus an aligned offset; fetching validates cached pool count bounds, pool presence and nonzero reference before exposing the entry array.
Fetching returns the entry count and array pointer, or zero on disabled storage, empty handle or corrupt handle; formatting and printing wrappers emit output only when entries exist.
Corrupt pool index, missing pool, or zero reference triggers a warning and a null result, documented as possible use after release or handle corruption.
Freelist reuse only recycles the least-recently-used head after its recorded grace state has passed; otherwise allocation falls back to pool space.
Record footprint covers the header plus requested entries aligned to depot granularity, with a check against maximum entry storage.
Diagnostic buffer, teardown report and sequential rendering use a display bound of sixteen entries; stack formatting uses an indent width of four.
